title: Patch friction scorecard + go-live notes — May 2026
content:
Quick summary:
This is a working scorecard and run notes doc for the May 2026 patch (small feature/bug cohort). Purpose: give launch leads a concise friction-oriented checklist, an hour-by-hour runpad for go-live, and a post-release mini-retrospective template.

Why this doc exists (context):
- Recent rollouts have shown transient tail-latency spikes in mid-traffic windows; engineering suspects interaction between autoscaler warm-up and model routing caches.
- This patch contains a small-serving runtime tweak (KV-cache eviction order) + a control-plane flag to prefer lower-cost kernels for some quantized variants.
- We expect modest traffic exposure (canary to 2% -> 20% over 3h), but want deterministic rollback hooks and explicit friction thresholds.

Goals for this rollout:
- Safely validate that kernel-selection fallback does not increase 95p latency by >10% on p99 windows.
- Ensure autoscaling doesn't create cold-cache storms for long-tail requests.
- Preserve customer-visible error-rate delta < 0.05% during the experiment.

Scorecard (quick telemetry signals to watch):
- Frontend p50/p95/p99 latency (route-specific): baseline vs canary. Thresholds: p95 increase >8% -> alert; p99 increase >12% -> immediate throttle.
- Token generation CPU/GPU utilization by pool: if any pool saturates >85% for >2m -> scale-back to prior config.
- Error rate (5xx plus inference-specific errors): +0.05% absolute increase -> pause rollout.
- Model mismatch / output regression (eval harness): any failure in golden prompt set for canary -> immediate rollback.
- Cold-cache rate: frequency of prefix miss events per-second. If miss rate > baseline*2 for >5m -> rollback.

Preflight checklist (to be completed before starting canary):
- [ ] Release PR merged and smoke tests green (CI link in PR).
- [ ] All required infra migrations applied (DB indices, config flags deployed to control-plane).
- [ ] Canary policy created in Console: target 2% traffic, 1 region (us-west1), 3h ramp.
- [ ] Observability: dashboards pinned and alerts configured (links posted in #releases channel).
- [ ] Pager roster for the 3h window assigned (lead, SRE, runtime eng, product liaison).
- [ ] Rollback runbook validated with on-call (simulated rollback dry-run earlier in day).
- [ ] Stakeholders notified (customer-success for affected customers).

Go-live runpad (hour-by-hour, concise):
- T-minus 30m: Final smoke run: run smoke script against canary control plane (smoke.sh) — expect passes.
- T-minus 15m: Post change readiness call (10m) — confirm pager coverage, thresholds, and patch notes.
- T=0: Create canary allocation (2%). Start sampling metrics and begin canary.
- T+15m: Quick check-in. If all green, continue. If marginal (scorecard warnings), hold and investigate.
- T+30m: Increase to 5% if no issues. If minor anomalies (p95 +6% but p99 stable), hold and observe another 30m.
- T+60m: Evaluate model-eval harness output. If any regression, rollback.
- T+90m: Ramp to 10% if green.
- T+150m: Ramp to 20% (final exposure) if green.
- T+180m: End experiment and decide: promote to stable, extend canary, or rollback.

In-run decision ladder (who decides what):
- Autothrottle (safety): triggered by automated alert threshold -> immediate reduce to previous traffic (SRE policy).
- Engineering lead (Evelyn): can pause ramp for non-critical anomalies and request 30m hold.
- On-call SRE: can execute rollback for severe infra signals (sustained saturation or error spike).
- Product PM (Priya): decides to abort if output quality regression is customer-impacting.

Throttle & rollback triggers (explicit):
- Immediate rollback: p99 latency > baseline + 20% for >3m, or error rate increase >0.2% absolute, or model eval failure.
- Pause + investigate: p95 latency > baseline + 10% for >5m, or cold-cache rate >2x baseline for >10m, or any unexplained allocation spike.
- Auto-throttle: pool utilization >90% for >2m triggers autoscale fallback and traffic reduction to prior stable.

Quick runbook snippets (commands):
- Create canary: ./release_ctl create-canary --config releases/may-2026/patch-friction.json --percent 2 --region us-west1
- Rollback: ./release_ctl rollback --target canary-id --to-tag stable-2026-04-28 
- Reduce traffic: ./release_ctl set-percent --canary canary-id --percent 1
- Check smoke logs: tail -n 500 /var/log/release-smoke/canary-<id>.log

Communication templates (post to #releases):
- Start: "[RELEASE START] May patch canary 2% at us-west1. Lead: Evelyn Park. Pager: Diego Ramos. Scorecard thresholds posted at <dashboard link>."
- Pause/hold: "[RELEASE HOLD] Pausing ramp at T+30 due to elevated p95 (details linked). Investigating — SRE on it."
- Rollback: "[ROLLBACK] Rolling back canary <id> to stable tag stable-2026-04-28. Root cause: <summary>. Follow-up: postmortem scheduled."

Post-release notes (template for quick fill):
- Release tag: patch-friction-2026-05-03
- Canary windows and final exposure: 2% -> 20% over 3h (regions: us-west1 only)
- Incidents triggered: none / describe if any
- Telemetry deltas: p95 +3%, p99 +1% (compared to baseline), error rate delta +0.01%
- Actions taken: ramp paused at T+30 for 18m while SRE trimmed autoscale config; resumed and completed ramp.
- Outcome: promoted to stable / rolled back (choose outcome).
- Follow-ups: list of tickets and owners (e.g., REL-789 -> Diego; INFRA-433 -> Samir)

Mini-retro prompts (to be filled within 48h):
- What was the closest-to-production friction point we observed?
- Were our thresholds too loose or too tight?
- Did we have the right telemetry pinned? Anything missing?
- One change to do before the next small patch (action owner + ETA).

Open risks & mitigations (notes for this patch):
- Risk: kernel fallback may increase tail latency under specific sequence lengths. Mitigation: add targeted evals with long-tail prompt set; pre-warm a small subset of pools during ramp.
- Risk: autoscaler config defaults during canary may differ across regions. Mitigation: single-region canary + ensure config parity script ran.

Notes-to-self / leftover TODOs:
- Confirm Confluence page CONF-5543 has final runbook embed (Evelyn).
- Add a condensed ops checklist to Console (Diego).
- Post-release: run the golden-prompt diff report and attach to ticket REL-789 (Priya).
- Follow up on kernel telemetry dashboard (Samir).

Appendix: quick checklist for on-call during ramp (copyable):
- Monitor dashboards: inference-latency, pool-utilization, error-rate, eval-failures.
- If any alert fires, mention the canary tag and timeframe in the incident title.
- If rollback executed, preserve artifacts (logs, trace links, sample requests) and tag PR with the incident id.

----
Draft status: this is a living document — refine after the first dry-run. If you add a note, append your initials and date (e.g., "EP 2026-05-03").
